The official Rust blog has a post announcing Rust 1.100.0 on November 12, 2026, which is the stable release you're asking about.

- **Official announcement:** The Rust Release Team published the announcement of a new version of Rust, 1.100.0. Existing users can upgrade through rustup with the stable channel update command.
- **Headline features:** The post lists the never type, the Allocator API, and the DropGuard API as stabilized. It says the never type is now stable after a long effort, and that this release changes Infallible to be an alias to the never type.
- **Independent coverage:** LWN reports that Cargo can also now set a minimum age for dependencies, to stop supply chain attacks, and can point out unused dependencies more reliably.
- **Compatibility caveat:** A third-party GitHub page (not official) warns that scripts comparing version strings as text or decimals may misread 1.100 as older than 1.99. It recommends testing under the beta toolchain before the release date. That page is unofficial, so treat its advice as a heads-up rather than an official guidance.

content.text:
The latest stable release of Rust is **1.100.0**, announced on November 12, 2026.

The official [Rust blog announcement](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/11/12/Rust-1.100.0/) confirms it. [LWN.net](https://lwn.net/Articles/1107188/) also covers the release.

The earlier search had shown 1.96 and 1.97 as the newest versions, but those results were stale. Rust ships a new stable version every six weeks, so 1.100.0 is the expected release for this date.

One heads-up: because the version number now has three digits, scripts that compare versions as text may treat 1.100 as older than 1.99. An [unofficial GitHub page](https://github.com/CyberNative-AI/what-breaks-next/releases/tag/2026-11-12-rust-1-100) flags this issue.
